intro: Using Notion for recruitment coordinators on Mac helps you manage high volumes of candidate data without the usual manual friction. You can build a central hub that tracks every stage of your hiring pipeline while keeping your notes, scorecards, and schedules in one place.
tldr: Use Notion databases to track candidate status from application to offer.
Leverage keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ P to navigate your workspace quickly.
Keep your Mac clean by using the Notion desktop app instead of browser tabs.
Ask Lazur to guide you through complex database setups or formula creation.
Automate your interview scorecards with reusable database templates.

blocks.text: Start by installing the Notion desktop app. Ensure you are on macOS 13 or later. Open the app and press ⌘ N to create a new page. Use this for your master candidate tracker. A database is the best way to handle hundreds of applicants. Type /database to get started with a Table view.

Add properties for Name, Email, Status, and Interview Date. Use Select or Status properties for your pipeline stages. This allows you to filter and sort your data easily. If you need to see who is in the final round, use the Filter button in the top right. Select your Status property and check only the Final Interview box.

Stop using messy documents for feedback. Create a database template for your interviews. Click the arrow next to the blue New button in your database. Select + New template. Name it Interview Scorecard. Add your standard questions inside this page. Now, every time you add a new candidate, you can click this template to fill it out instantly.

items: Use the Select property for interview ratings to keep data consistent.
Add a Date property to track when the interview took place.
Link your candidates to a separate Job Openings database using the Relation property.
Use the Rollup property to see how many candidates are currently in a specific role.

blocks.text: Recruitment coordinators move fast. Don't let the mouse slow you down. Press ⌘ P to open the search bar. This is the fastest way to jump between candidate pages. Use ⌘ ⌥ ⌃ ⇧ to close the sidebar and gain more screen space. Press ⇧ ? to see the full list of Notion shortcuts on your Mac.
If you are stuck on a complex formula, ask Lazur to explain how to write it. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask: How do I calculate the days since the last candidate update in Notion?
blocks.title: Get help with formulas

blocks.text: The scheduling tax is the time spent on back and forth emails. Integrate your calendar links directly into your candidate profile templates. When you create a candidate page, your booking link is already there. Copy and paste it into your email template. This saves you from hunting for links in your browser.
Working with Lazur on your Mac

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It is ready to help when you are overwhelmed. If you need to find a specific setting in Notion, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where it is. Lazur will draw a circle around the menu item. If you need to write a rejection email, use dictation. Hold the fn key and speak your draft. Lazur turns your voice into clean, formatted text right in the Notion block.

Large pipelines can be hard to visualize. Try the Board view for your candidates. Click the + button in your database view and select Board. Group the board by Status. Now you can drag and drop candidates as they move through your process. This view is excellent for morning standups with hiring managers.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for applicant tracking?
faq.answer: Yes, Notion works well as a lightweight applicant tracking system for small to mid-sized teams. Use databases to manage candidate stages, scorecards, and job descriptions.

faq.question: How do I speed up Notion on my Mac?
faq.answer: Use the dedicated desktop app rather than a browser tab. Press ⌘ R to reload if the app feels sluggish. Ensure your macOS is up to date.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Notion?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your entire Mac screen. It can guide you through Notion menus, explain how to use specific features, and dictate text into any Notion block.

faq.question: What is the best way to share candidate feedback?
faq.answer: Create a template for interview scorecards. Share the specific page with the hiring manager so they can add their comments directly to the candidate profile.
